purpose: Momelotinib is used to treat a bone marrow disease called myelofibrosis in adults who have anemia (low red blood cell counts). It helps control the disease and can reduce the need for blood transfusions. It is used in patients who have already been treated with another JAK inhibitor or who are starting treatment for the first time.
how_it_works: Your bone marrow has proteins called JAK1 and JAK2 that send signals telling cells to grow. In myelofibrosis, these signals go haywire and cause problems like scarring of the bone marrow and low blood counts. Momelotinib blocks these overactive signals to help slow the disease and also blocks another protein called ACVR1 that contributes to anemia, helping your body make more red blood cells.
common_side_effects: Feeling dizzy or lightheaded, nausea, low platelet counts (which can increase bleeding risk), low white blood cell counts (which can raise infection risk), diarrhea, headache, fatigue, and increased liver enzymes seen on blood tests.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have fever, chills, or signs of infection. It can lower your blood counts, so regular blood tests are needed. There is a risk of blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. It may increase your risk of certain cancers including lymphoma and skin cancer, so limit sun exposure. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 200 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not crush or split the tablet. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your blood counts or side effects.
